context.body: Noah’s entry becomes a temporal boundary inside teaching about an unknown future hour.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Jesus says the day and hour are unknown and compares the Son of Man’s coming with ordinary life continuing until Noah entered the ship.
observations.label: Jesus compares his coming with Noah’s days: action

observations.body: The flood arrives unexpectedly, and the comparison leads to watchfulness and readiness.
observations.label: Jesus compares his coming with Noah’s days: response

observations.body: days of Noah · eating and drinking · did not know · watch · be ready
observations.label: Words in Matthew 24:36–44

payload.posture: Read Matthew 24:36–44 as warning, faith, and water evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The comparison emphasizes unexpected arrival; it does not make every detail of the flood a direct prediction.
payload.title: Jesus compares his coming with Noah’s days
